title: Add a shared soundness question to the critic and verifier briefs
summary: Define one soundness-question string in briefs.rs and put it in both the critic brief and every change-verifier brief. It asks whether a careful senior engineer would reject the approach as a crude heuristic, an unneeded special case, a guess where code or data could be read, or a rule with obvious false positives, and it names the better alternative. Tests with fake critic and verifier outputs show that a blocker soundness finding makes the plan verdict revise and fails the verifier verdict even when all criteria are met, and that minor findings change neither. Audience: the Athena maintainer.

defaults_applied.how: Add fake-output tests for critic and verifier; require fmt, clippy -D warnings and cargo test to pass.
Criteria check the verdict outcomes from fake outputs, not that the text exists.
The shared const makes the wording drift-proof, and the existing blocker/major gates enforce the verdict.
One shared question covers both gates instead of separate wording in each.
The check is that a crude-but-criteria-meeting design is no longer passed.
One focused change over the six named files.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Existing rules already make blocker or major findings block a verifier pass (verify.rs) and force revise from the critic (run/mod.rs), so the work is the shared question text plus tests that pin this behaviour for soundness findings.

The question text lives as one shared const in briefs.rs and is rendered into both briefs, so the verifier prompt file (2 tokens of headroom) grows little or not at all; critic.md has 517 tokens of room.
Soundness findings are ordinary findings with a blocker, major, minor or nit severity; no new severity or output schema field is added.
The soundness check covers the approach only, not style, and the question is added only to change verification (the study verifier is untouched).
The CHANGELOG entry follows the existing format.

acceptance_criteria.text: briefs.rs defines the soundness question once, and both the critic brief and the change-verifier brief render that same constant. It asks about a crude heuristic, a special case that should be general, a guess where code or data could be read, and a rule with obvious false positives. It requires naming every such problem with the simpler or more correct alternative, and it is limited to approach, not style.
Run `cargo test`: the brief tests assert the critic brief and the change-verifier brief both contain the identical soundness question text, and the existing prompt size/token-limit test passes.
Run `cargo test`: a test with a fake critic output carrying a blocker soundness finding yields plan verdict revise, and one with only a minor soundness finding does not change the verdict.

Run `cargo test`: a test with a fake verifier output carrying a blocker soundness finding, with all criteria met, yields a failed verdict, and a minor soundness finding leaves a passing verdict passing.
Run `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: both are clean. `cargo test` passes for the whole workspace.
CHANGELOG.md has a new entry describing the soundness question in the critic and verifier. No governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml) change.

out_of_scope: Adding a new severity level or output schema field
departures: Slightly higher cost and time than the reference: the change touches prompts under tight token budgets and needs tests in two crates.
urgent_reason: It cuts wasted work from crude designs that pass verification, land, and then have to be redone.
hard_reason: It changes the critic's revise rule and the verifier's pass/fail gate that judges other jobs.
